create.title: Hard-TOP phase alignment and product-fibre mean obstruction
create.statement_tex: For finite row supports S_m, arbitrary real phases phi_(m,h), a unit-modulus direction c_h, and coefficients |a_(m,h)|<=1, the exact variational identity is sup_a sum_m |sum_(h in S_m) a_(m,h)e(phi_(m,h))c_h|^2=sum_m |S_m|^2. A hard-cone rectangle retains asymptotic L entries per row after every hm-square entry is deleted, so this support-phase-magnitude class has Hilbert-Schmidt energy asymptotic L^2 and selected energy asymptotic L^3. After the phase and character are absorbed, averaging along exact product fibres is genuinely noninvertible but fixes every F(m,h)=f(mh), including the coherent constant direction; its complementary high-pass kills that direction and requires a remainder of full coherent capacity. Hence support, pointwise magnitude, the displayed joint phase, and product-fibre averaging cannot prove the L^2X^epsilon nonsquare target. This is a coefficient-interface obstruction, not a lower bound for the literal endpoint array; a continuation must use a proved actual-coefficient property that fails under entrywise phase alignment and must control the discarded fibre mean.
create.next_action: Keep hard TOP parked at the nonsquare actual direction. Reopen only with the literal endpoint formula and a structural lemma excluding entrywise phase alignment, together with a target-safe estimate of the discarded product-fibre mean.

create.title: Lower centered square-function and Farey determinant self-return
create.statement_tex: For the exact Round-122 increment S(k)=I_k V_delta and c_y=sum_(d<=y)chi_4(d)/d, the uncentered dyadic energy is false at target capacity: on a positive block K asymptotic y, the actual drift kc_y gives sum_(K<k<=2K)|S(k)|^2 >> y^3. The unique centering is S^circ(k)=S(k)-kc_y, and the original scalar wavelet is target-equivalent to its centered form because its exact full first moment vanishes and the central and far truncations are target-safe. The sufficient estimate sum_(k in K(K))|S^circ(k)|^2 << K(R^2+K)X^epsilon is a stronger separated k-norm and at K=y asks for y^2 against coefficient-blind y^3 capacity. The broader centered discrepancy has an exact reduced-Farey expansion with coefficient lambda_b=chi_4(b)b^(-1)sum_(g<=y/b)chi_4(g)/g; the b=1 term is exactly the centre, determinant zero is equality of reduced fractions and contributes O(K(y+K)X^epsilon), while all missing cancellation lies in the prescribed-centre nonzero determinant. The expansion is an ambient Fourier canonicalization and provides no gain. This obstruction does not disprove a genuinely signed scalar inequality for the actual wavelet.
create.next_action: Do not use the uncentered norm, a separated positive k-square function, or ambient Farey spectrum as the claimed gain. Reopen lower GAR only with a genuinely signed scalar inequality that keeps the wavelet index joint with the low-two-adic and complementary labels.

create.title: Critical scalar-cell prescribed-centre continuation has no strict saving
create.statement_tex: At W=Y^(7/16), write a=log_Y(D/L). Even granting every literal determinant cell the prescribed-centre scalar envelope Y^epsilon min(Y^a,Y^((1-a)/2)) with no interface loss, the triangular cell square function has exponent beta_scalar(a)=2min(a,(1-a)/2)+max(0,7/16-a). At the complete critical block D=Y^(1/2), L=Y^(1/6), one has a=1/3 and beta_scalar=37/48, exactly the strongest certified complete capacity. Thus scalar-per-cell continuation cannot produce a uniform strict power saving, even before floors, stars, moving symbols, and endpoint transfer are charged. This is a capacity obstruction to that mechanism, not a lower bound for the actual determinant correlation.
create.next_action: Park scalar-per-cell prescribed-centre continuation at the a=1/3 contact. Any strict graded saving must couple cells or keep the lift endpoint inside the same reciprocal window before a norm.

create.title: Conditional local transverse lift square-variation connector
create.statement_tex: At W=Y^(7/16), D=Y^(1/2), L=Y^(1/6), let B=Y^b with 1/3<=b<=1/2, Q_B=min(B,BD/(WL)), lambda_B=YL/(DB^2), and J_B=1+DQ_B/B^2. Suppose every literal complete lift amplitude U_(i,rho) on the actual reciprocal q-window satisfies ||U_(i,rho)||_(V^2(I)) << Y^epsilon J_B^(1/2)/L, including all smooth, hard, floor, star, endpoint, support-birth, and moving-symbol pieces. Suppose also its unseparated reciprocal sum obeys the V^2-weighted curvature inequality |sum_(v in I)^* U_(i,rho)(v)e(-ca'/(kappa_i rho v)+vartheta_i rho v)| << ||U_(i,rho)||_(V^2(I)) min(N_rho,N_rho sqrt(lambda_B rho^2)+(lambda_B rho^2)^(-1/2))Y^epsilon, without an extra N_rho^(1/2). Then the complete B-shell is O_epsilon(D J_B^(1/2)min(Q_B,Q_Bsqrt(lambda_B)+lambda_B^(-1/2))Y^epsilon), and summing all shells gives O_epsilon(Y^(73/96+epsilon)), a strict Y^(1/96) improvement over Y^(37/48+epsilon). Both hypotheses are open. The conditional exponent gives persistence 115/288>1/3, so it banks only a fixed-block saving and does not improve the global theorem.
create.next_action: First prove or refute the literal local V^2 coefficient norm J_B^(1/2)/L. Only if it passes, test the joint curvature inequality; stop on full-shell variation, J_B^theta with theta>=2/3, an N_rho^(1/2) loss, or owner separation.

Exact product-fibre means fix F(m,h)=f(mh), including the coherent aligned direction; a high-pass needs a full-capacity remainder.
The aligned array chooses adversarial phases and does not establish that the literal endpoint coefficient has large energy.
The actual drift kc_y produces energy much larger than y^2 on a block K asymptotic y.
Cauchy discards cross-k signs and creates a stronger separated positive norm.
The exact transform retains y^3 coefficient-blind capacity at K=y; only the diagonal is target-safe and the nonzero determinant is unproved.
At D/L=Y^(1/3), its square-function exponent is exactly 37/48.
Replacing the local birth count J_B by the full lift length D/B erases the Y^(1/96) margin.
Its persistence exponent is 115/288, which is worse than the already proved one-third theorem.
Both the literal local V^2 coefficient norm and the joint V^2-weighted curvature inequality remain open.
